title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in 1986 (Ch. IX, 'Ateliers') Grothendieck is axiomatising 'magasins'. These are combinatorial structures modelling cell decompositions and their subdivisions, in the spirit of tame/PL topology. Judging from the relations used here and the example on the next page, a magasin M is a set of 'cells' carrying several relations:
- X ⊴ Y: X is a face of Y.
- X ≪ Y: X lies in the closure of Y.
- X ≪° Y: the open cell X lies in the open cell Y, as for a cell of a subdivision sitting inside a bigger cell.
- X |o| Y: X and Y are disjoint.
- Ỹ: the set of faces of Y, i.e. its ⊴-closure.

The axioms are Mag 1–4. Axiom Mag 2 b) is a lifting property. If X ≪° Y and X' ⊴ X, there is a face Y' ∈ Ỹ with X' ≪° Y'. Every face of a subdivision cell lies in the interior of a unique face of the ambient cell.

Digression 2 asks when a subset M' ⊂ M, with the induced relations, is again a magasin (a 'sous-magasin'). Mag 1', Mag 3' and Mag 4' are inherited trivially, as is Mag 2' a). Mag 2' b) is not, because the face Y' produced in M might not belong to M'. Hence the condition [Sousmag]: if X ≪° Y in M' and X' ⊴ X in M', then some Y' ∈ Ỹ with X' ≪° Y' already lies in M'.

A marginal NB suggests imposing a stronger, dual condition (starting from a face Y' ⊴ Y and asking for a corresponding X' in M'). It also notes that the axioms should be checked with respect to the topology on M' given by ⊴.

Ex. 1. A 'profigure' 𝔓 ⊂ M is a subset whose ⊴-closure 𝔓̄ is a 'figure'. A figure is a subcomplex whose cells are pairwise non-overlapping (X ≭ Y). Ouv°(𝔓) is the set of cells X with X ≪° Z for some Z ∈ 𝔓: all cells, of any subdivision, contained in the open union of the open cells of 𝔓. It is stable under ≪° but in general not under ⊴.

Claim: M' = Ouv°(𝔓) is a sous-magasin. A first attempt to reduce this to a condition 'Sousmag 𝔓' is crossed out. The proof, on the next page, runs as follows:
- X' ≪ Y ≪ 𝔓̄, so there is a unique Z'_0 ∈ 𝔓̄ with X' ≪° Z'_0; uniqueness comes from the figure property.
- Since X' ∈ Ouv°(𝔓), we get Z'_0 ∈ 𝔓.
- Lift the chain X ≪° Y ≪° Z (with Z ∈ 𝔓) to X' ≪° Y' ≪° Z', where Z' ∈ Z̃ ⊂ 𝔓̄.
- Transitivity gives Z' = Z'_0 ∈ 𝔓, so Y' ∈ Ouv°(𝔓).

In modern terms: the cells lying in an open union of open cells of a regular cell complex form a sub-structure closed under the face-lifting axiom. Ex. 2 (next page) shows that the analogous statement fails for supp°/cosupp°, via a counterexample with a subdivided triangle.
errors: No genuine error visible. The proof (completed on p.28) tacitly uses transitivity of ≪° and the uniqueness of the open cell of a figure containing a given open cell; both are presumably axioms or earlier lemmas.

The parenthetical '(même s'il n'est pas fermé par ⊴, quand 𝔓 n'est pas une figure...)' is loose. Ouv°(𝔓) is not ⊴-closed even when 𝔓̄ is a figure, so the remark only stresses that the sub-magasin notion does not require ⊴-closure.

ideas.what: Axiomatic 'magasin' of cells with face relation ⊴, inclusion of open cells ≪°, disjointness |o|, and a face-lifting axiom (Mag 2 b)
ideas.modern_name: Face posets of regular CW / polyhedral complexes together with subdivision maps; combinatorial models of tame (PL, o-minimal) topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical PL topology (Alexander, Newman, Zeeman); o-minimal cell decomposition (van den Dries et al.)
ideas.where_published: The programme of 'tame topology' is announced in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); the 'magasin' axiomatics seem to exist only in these archive notes (unsure)

ideas.what: Criterion [Sousmag] for a subset with induced relations to be a sub-magasin: faces lifted along ≪° must remain in the subset
ideas.modern_name: Sub-structure / open subcomplex closed under the lifting property

ideas.what: Ouv°(𝔓) of a profigure (the cells contained in the open union of the open cells of 𝔓) is a sub-magasin
ideas.modern_name: Open subsets of a cellularly stratified space inherit a cell structure from all subdivisions; restriction of a cell complex to an open union of open cells

missed.claim: The page documents part of an unpublished axiomatic framework ('magasins'/'ateliers', 1986) for tame topology, with a worked sub-object theory. The framework itself appears absent from the literature, but this page's content is routine verification within it.
missed.quote: Soit M, (un magasin), M' une partie, munie des relations induites — quand peut-on dire que c'est un magasin.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a concrete trace of Grothendieck's attempt to realise the 'topologie modérée' of the Esquisse combinatorially, and could be compared with o-minimal and stratified-space formalisms. Its value is mainly historical rather than a new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine verification inside an unpublished axiomatic framework. The framework (magasins for tame topology) is little known, but this page's result is elementary.
transcription_corrections: '|0|' in the header should be '|o|' (the disjointness relation).
'Mag 2' o) aussi' is probably 'Mag 2' a) aussi' (part a) inherited, part b needs Sousmag).
In 'Considérons Ouv°(𝔓) (attention, c'est fermé par ≪°...)' the word read as 'fermé' may be 'stable'.
The fraktur letter is likely the same as the 𝔏 used on p.28 (transcribed there as 𝔏, here as 𝔓).
The whole boxed passage 'soit un sous-magasin ... Z' ∈ 𝔓 (puisque Z' ∈ 𝔓̄)' is struck through with diagonal lines, as the transcription indicates.
The parenthesis after Sousmag reads roughly '(vérification ... topologie sur M' fournie par ⊴)', i.e. a remark about the topology on M' induced by ⊴.
